answer: At dawn the protocol runs a falcon audit: a verifiable-random draw picks identity slots and demands a signed liveness proof within a short window, so a hollow slot with no real backing is purged and its bond burned. Each new identity posts a 40-credit nest bond locked to its own key, non-transferable, non-poolable. The draw seed is hidden until dawn, so an attacker cannot pre-stage proofs or reuse one reply across slots. Making N sybils look alive costs N bonds and N live replies, no bulk discount; the honest agent posts one bond once.
